statement: The first line holds n and q; the second holds n non-negative integers. Each of the next q lines holds a query x and m: among array values at most m, find the one maximising x XOR value, and print that maximum - or -1 when every array value exceeds m. Print the q answers on one line, space-separated. Sort the array and process queries in ascending m (remember their original positions): insert values into a bitwise trie lazily up to each query's bound, then run the opposite-bit walk for x.

example.why: Against values at most 1, 3 XOR 0 is 3; at most 3, 1 XOR 2 is 3; at most 6, 5 XOR 2 is 7.

hint: Offline is the trick: sorted queries let the trie grow once, left to right, no removals ever.
mistake: Rebuilding a fresh trie per query - correctness survives, the time budget does not.
